finding.evidence: The test builds `const source = `<img${' '.repeat(100_000)}`` — an `<img` followed by *trailing* whitespace and nothing else. markdown-it's block paragraph rule sets `token.content = state.getLines(...).trim()`, so the inline state's `src` is `'<img'` with the 100k spaces already gone before `imgRule`/`IMG_TAG_RE` ever runs. As written the assertions (`not.toContain('<img')` is true for plain escaped text regardless, and `elapsed < 1000ms` on a ~4-char inline string) hold whether the fix in `img-plugin.ts` is present or reverted, so the perf guard this diff exists to install has no test that can fail. verdict.reason: The test exists as described and is vacuous. `img-plugin.test.ts:148` builds `<img` + 100k *trailing* spaces; `render()` (lines 15-17) uses `new MarkdownIt({ html: false })`, so with html_block disabled the line is handled by markdown-it v14's paragraph rule (package.json:65 pins ^14.1.0), which assigns `token.content = state.getLines(...).trim()`. The whitespace run is stripped before inline parsing, so `imgRule` (img-plugin.ts:148-151) receives `state.src === '<img'` and both the new `IMG_TAG_RE` (img-plugin.ts:64) and the reverted two-quantifier regex described at img-plugin.ts:56-62 fail in constant time. Consequently `expect(html).not.toContain('<img')` (true for any escaped fallback) and `expect(elapsed).toBeLessThan(1_000)` (a 4-char render) both hold whether or not the fix is present — the perf guard this diff installs has no test that can fail. No other test constructs the triggering shape (an interior whitespace run followed by a failing continuation): the nearest, lines 158-165, uses a short string and only asserts text survival, and a package-wide grep for `repeat(`/`performance.now` finds perf guards only in remote-selection.test.ts and preview.test.ts, unrelated to IMG_TAG_RE. Squarely in the test-adequacy lane and major: a reverted ReDoS fix would ship green, and the plugin runs inside a synchronous render on collaborator-authored notes.
